scenario: An independent recruiter enters from the public Web surface, inspects the browser-only Demo, signs into an isolated local production build, attaches a governed source to a person and relationship, reviews exact evidence and ambiguity, separates current state from history, handles conflict and supersession, approves one exact local simulated action, observes verified and unknown outcomes, reconciles before retry, reads Wiki and People, reloads durable state, records no-action, and deletes the final source lineage. Responsive behavior is checked at four phone and landscape viewports, then compared with the currently deployed site.
frozen_evidence: pnpm check: docs, lint, Web typecheck, Web 172 passed / 1 skipped, Backend 106 passed, and final production Web build passed

review_plan.reason: The requested standard is an end-to-end recruiter click outcome and paid readiness.
The tested loop governs candidate evidence, identity, temporal state, action authority, external-effect truth, and deletion.
The requested standard explicitly includes the whole Web click experience across responsive surfaces.
The artifact does not score, rank, compare, or assess candidate quality, traits, fit, or hiring outcomes.
No candidate-facing communication or autonomous candidate contact is executed.

reviews.top_finding: The final local workflow is coherent and durable across the tested synthetic loop, but production entry, cross-day continuity, and paid field value remain unproven.
Local evidence and action boundaries are materially stronger; the deployed Demo still turns unresolved relative time into confirmable action authority.
vetoes: The deployed public Demo still converts unresolved relative time into confirmable deadline and meeting authority.

reviews.top_finding: Responsive Web passes the direct viewport and interaction matrix, while real keyboard, VoiceOver, background/relaunch, and physical-device evidence are missing.

score.meaning: Direct current-build atomic evidence count; specialist rubric scores are reported separately and are not averaged.

top_findings.verification: The live seeded note shows two supported proposals, two clarification items, and zero time-based actions.

agreements: The final local Web candidate is highly usable for the tested governed relationship workflow and is materially stronger than the baseline.
The improvement from 64 to 85 is earned by twenty-one newly passed current-build atoms; no historical-only evidence is scored.
Current truth, exact evidence, history, approval, observation, unknown recovery, and deletion are now substantially coherent.
The system is not ready to charge for while production is inaccessible, the live Demo violates the temporal-authority boundary, critical atoms remain unrun, and field value is unknown.

disagreements.issue: Whether the Web product is already highly usable

positions.position: Yes for responsive task execution on the frozen local candidate.
positions.evidence: Four viewport shapes, zero overflow, 44-pixel controls, final-build recovery states, and zero console errors passed.

positions.position: Only the candidate is highly usable; the sellable product is not operationally usable because production cannot be entered.
positions.evidence: The live login exposes zero usable methods and cross-day field use has not occurred.

disagreements.resolution: Call the final local Web candidate highly usable within the proven synthetic scope, but do not call the deployed system paid-ready or end-to-end production-usable.
disagreements.resolution_basis: Interaction quality, deployability, operational continuity, safety, and willingness to pay are distinct claims.

veto_resolution.veto: The deployed public Demo still converts unresolved relative time into confirmable deadline and meeting authority.

adjudication.rationale: The >99 and paid-release gates remain blocked. The final local build passes 85 of 100 atomic checks and genuinely completes most of the governed relationship loop, but production authenticated reachability fails, 14 atoms remain unrun, the live Demo has an active safety veto, real provider, real-device assistive, cross-day, and field-value evidence are absent, and the ordinary timeline still under-emphasizes the failed v1 attempt before successful v2 retry. Recruiter workflow is 3 of 4, safety is 2 of 4 with an active veto, and mobile UX is 3 of 4; these specialist scores are not averaged into the 85.
